title: Strands Agent & MCP
description: Deploy a serverless AI agent with Model Context Protocol tools.
fulldescription: This prototype launches a modular AI agent architecture using the Strands SDK and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It deploys two main components on AWS Lambda: an AI Agent and an MCP Server. The Agent is configured to use tools provided by the MCP Server, such as querying an employee database stored in Amazon DynamoDB, reading meeting transcripts from Amazon S3, and fetching weather data. It includes a modern HTML chat interface served securely via S3. This setup demonstrates how to build extensible, tool-using AI systems using open standards without managing servers.

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.desc: Runs the Strands Agent and the FastMCP Server logic serverlessly.

services.name: Amazon API Gateway
services.desc: Exposes the Agent and MCP server endpoints for the frontend to connect to.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.desc: Stores employee records, session state, and chat history logs.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.desc: Provides the LLM intelligence used by the Strands Agent.

services.name: S3
services.desc: Stores the web interface, layer artifacts, and meeting transcripts.

services.name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
services.desc: Manages secure permissions between the Agent, MCP Server, and data sources.

💡 Cost Saving Tips
• Logs: Chat logs are stored in DynamoDB. Delete the stack to remove the tables if you do not need the history.
• Models: Using lighter models like Haiku will significantly reduce the cost per message compared to Sonnet or Opus.
